seoTitle: Regex URL Tester: Check a Pattern Against Many URLs
metaDescription: Test one regular expression against a list of URLs and see matches, non-matches, capture groups and a replacement preview. For redirects and filters.
intro: Enter a regular expression and a list of URLs. See which URLs match, what the capture groups hold and what a replacement such as /articles/$2 would produce.
why:
Redirect rules and analytics filters often use regular expressions, and a pattern that looks right can miss URLs or match too many. Testing against a real list of URLs catches that before the rule goes live.

This uses JavaScript regular expression syntax. Apache (PCRE), Nginx and Google Analytics have small differences, so re-check on the target system. A pattern with heavy backtracking can freeze the page: keep patterns simple.
howTo: Type the regex in the first box. A /pattern/flags form works too.
Choose what to test against: path, path and query, or full URL.
Optionally add a replacement to preview the redirect target.

faq.a: JavaScript. Most simple patterns behave the same in PCRE, but lookbehind, possessive quantifiers and some escapes differ.

faq.q: Should I test the path or the full URL?
faq.a: Redirect rules in Apache and Nginx see the path only. Analytics filters usually see the page path or the full URL.

faq.q: Why is a URL with a query string not matching?
faq.a: With "path only" the query is ignored. Switch to "path and query" if your pattern includes it.

faq.q: What does $1 mean in the replacement?
faq.a: The first capture group, in the same way as in Apache RedirectMatch.
